citation: Hanley, P., Böhnke, J. R., Slavin, B., Elliott, L., & Croudace, T. (2016). Let's Think Secondary Science: Evaluation report and executive summary. London: Education Endowment Foundation.
report_number: EEF project: Let's Think Secondary Science (LTSS); independent evaluation by the Institute for Effective Education, University of York; July 2016
design: Cluster RCT (assignment = School, matched-pair / minimisation within 3 regions); 53 secondary schools randomised (26 intervention / 27 control); analysed sample 47 schools (23 int / 24 ctrl) for the primary science outcome; ~8,016 pupils, Year 7-8 (KS3, ages 11-13, grade 7-12 band per registry); intervention = Let's Think Secondary Science (a cognitive-acceleration / CASE-derived science PD programme: teacher CPD + 19 one-hour LTSS lessons over Years 7-8); business-as-usual control; primary outcome = science attainment (KS3 SATs paper) at end of Year 8; secondary outcomes = English & maths (GL Assessment). Efficacy/effectiveness trial.
problems: Effect sizes are EEF cluster-randomised Hedges' g taken directly from the report (Table 3 primary, Table 4 secondary, Table 5 subgroup): g = between-school adjusted impact (gamma01, controlled for KS2 pre-test and gender) / sqrt(sigma_school^2 + sigma_error^2) (total variance). These already account for clustering, so cluster_adjusted=true. Impact SE not printed; derived from the reported 95% CI (SE = CI width / (2*1.96)); these CIs are bootstrapped, so the SE is an approximation and p-values are one-sided bootstrapped. I extracted the MAIN unweighted ITT models as the headline contrasts; the report also gives missingness-weighted sensitivity versions (science g=-0.02; English g=-0.13; maths g=-0.13) and a per-protocol science version (g=+0.01) -- recorded in notes, not as separate rows. The secondary maths/English analyses were under-powered (only 17 schools maths / 20 schools English, because each school administered only one of the two tests) and used one-sided tests aimed at detecting positive transfer, so their (negative) point estimates are not robust evidence of harm. ICCs recorded per outcome are the observed in-sample values (Tech Appendix Table 6); design-stage ICC was 0.12. Raw posttest means/SDs: report gives covariate-adjusted ('expected') means with 95% CIs but not raw posttest SDs, so mean_t/mean_c are the adjusted means and sd fields are left null. Note: registry row 42 lists SES as 'Average/High' and goal '(P)CK'; this matches the LTSS pedagogy/PCK focus though LTSS schools spanned a range of intakes. The exec-summary headline science effect (-0.02, -0.09 to 0.04) is the weighted model; the unweighted main model is -0.01 (-0.09 to 0.04).

effect_sizes.arm_label: Let's Think Secondary Science (single TPD arm) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: Science attainment test (KS3 science SATs, 2009 Tier 3-6 Paper 2; max 90)
effect_sizes.g_method: EEF cluster-randomised Hedges' g taken directly from report Table 3 (primary, main unweighted ITT model): g = adjusted between-school impact gamma01 (controlling for KS2 pre-test and gender) / sqrt(sigma_school^2 + sigma_error^2) (total variance). SE derived from reported bootstrapped 95% CI (-.09, .04): SE = (0.04-(-0.09))/(2*1.96); g_var = SE^2.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.18 Table 3 (row 'Science test', primary analysis); exec summary p.4 (headline -0.02 is the missingness-weighted variant)
effect_sizes.notes: Primary confirmatory outcome. Science -> STEM per spec. mean_t/mean_c are covariate-adjusted ('expected') means (95% CI 44.43-48.16 int; 44.92-47.93 ctrl); raw posttest SDs not reported. n in model = 5882 (3020 int; 2862 ctrl). One-sided bootstrapped p=0.75. Sensitivity variants on same sample: missingness-weighted g=-0.02 (-.10,.04); per-protocol g=+0.01 (-.08,.10). Observed ICC=0.129 (Tech Appendix Table 6); design-stage ICC=0.12. No evidence of impact on science attainment.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Let's Think Secondary Science (single TPD arm) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: GL Assessment Progress Test in English 13 (PTE)
effect_sizes.g_method: EEF cluster-randomised Hedges' g taken directly from report Table 4 (secondary, main unweighted model): g = adjusted between-school impact / sqrt(total variance), controlling for KS2 and test mode (online/paper). SE derived from reported bootstrapped 95% CI (-.24, -.06): SE = (-0.06-(-0.24))/(2*1.96); g_var = SE^2.
effect_sizes.notes: Secondary transfer outcome. English -> Reading per spec. Only 20 schools administered the English test (each school did either maths or English), so under-powered. One-sided bootstrapped p=0.99 (test designed to detect positive transfer only; negative estimate not robust evidence of harm). Adjusted means (95% CI 87.41-97.24 int; 90.35-97.66 ctrl); raw SDs not reported. n in model=2397 (964 int; 1433 ctrl). Missingness-weighted variant g=-0.13 (-.23,-.04). Observed ICC=0.156.

effect_sizes.g_method: EEF cluster-randomised Hedges' g taken directly from report Table 4 (secondary, main unweighted model): g = adjusted between-school impact / sqrt(total variance), controlling for KS2 and test mode. effect_sizes.test_name: Science attainment test (KS3 science SATs Paper 2) -- FSM subgroup
effect_sizes.g_method: EEF cluster-randomised Hedges' g taken directly from report Table 5 (subgroup): same model as primary, restricted to Ever-FSM pupils. SE derived from reported 95% CI (-.18, .06): SE = (0.06-(-0.18))/(2*1.96); g_var = SE^2.
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.20 Table 5 (row 'Science Test, FSM-only'); exec summary p.4 (LTSS FSM vs control -0.03, -0.18 to 0.07)
effect_sizes.notes: Non-randomised subgroup (Ever-FSM pupils), is_full_sample=false. Provided for completeness; not the headline contrast. n in model=1608 (783 int; 825 ctrl). p=0.84. Other reported subgroups not extracted: female students g=+0.10 (.03,.19), male g=-0.05 (-.13,.03), KS2 strata g=+0.02/+0.05/-0.04; the female-only positive effect was flagged by the authors as likely chance (multiple exploratory tests; no within-subgroup mean difference; below the MDES of 0.20).
